title: Globalization and International Trade
text: Globalization is the process of increasing interconnection of the world's economies, cultures, and populations, driven by cross-border trade in goods and services, technology, and flows of investment, people, and information. Modern globalization accelerated after World War II with trade liberalization, and again with the digital revolution and the rise of China as a manufacturing hub. It has contributed to significant economic growth, poverty reduction in developing countries, and lower consumer prices. Critics point to negative effects including job displacement in developed countries, exploitation of workers in developing countries, cultural homogenization, and increased vulnerability to global shocks like the 2008 financial crisis and COVID-19 pandemic.
